formulaMethod.reason: Full available logical CPU mask on an exclusively quiet machine follows the existing historical release protocol. Both single-core and two-core restrictions interfere with background WASM compilation; original binaries, default JIT flags and unchanged gates are retained.

coldRow.note: Against the portable-path 0.5.4 recapture. The baseline median is below 1 ms, so the release comparison gates the median only, with a 0.3 ms floor.

supersededTwoCpuColdRow.note: Earlier about-5% observations describe steady-state or isolated-row experiments, not this latest full cold pair.

pairedGate.fix: Own-checkout root is not a baseline engine root. The one-line fix and regression test land after the capture-results commit.

compilationDiagnostics.metric: Median total of first three timed samples with concurrentJIT=false; four processes per build
compilationDiagnostics.caveat: Diagnostic synchronous compilation is not the release cold-row median, not a statistically established steady-state first-bad commit, and not one commit explaining the gate failure. Outlining prototype rejected and unshipped; only benchmark workloads were checked.

xirr.method: 10 fresh-process ABBA blocks per context, one fixture warmup then five fresh timed samples per process; process medians summarized independently. Paired log-ratio bootstrap across blocks: 20,000 resamples, 99% interval. Not a release gate.

textLookup.classification: The superseded raw text lookup flag remains in the archived 4,6 capture. Existing paired and fresh-variant controls stayed within their budgets. Final full-affinity measurements are compared independently without suppressing flags.

handsontable.classification: All nine render-baseline flags affect the unchanged Handsontable control, not Sheetwrite. They show comparison-environment or harness uncertainty; the cause is not isolated. No normalization or flag suppression was applied.

regressionTriage.classification: The former XIRR flag is genuine deferred compilation interference under restricted CPU affinity, not a slower numeric XIRR implementation. Final release formula suites use the full available CPU mask. Final flags remain in the comparison metrics without suppression.

coldPrefixControls.classification: Both parse-load flags did not reproduce. Text lookup is slower in 0.6: about 4% (default engine, sorted) and 13% (full engine), within the 25% release budget.

publicationNotes.title: Reading the flags
paragraphs: Each flag compares one 0.6.0 capture with one fresh 0.5.4 capture of the same suite. A flag means that pair exceeded the suite's documented budget; it is not a controlled confirmation of a regression.

All nine `render-baseline.json` flags are Handsontable rows. Handsontable is the comparison control and is version 18.1.2 on both sides, so these flags reflect variation between the two capture sessions, not a Sheetwrite change. The cause is not isolated, and the rows are not normalized or suppressed. They also indicate how much render timing can move between sessions on this machine.
The aggregate `full-engine-results.json` table repeats three flags from the default and full formula tables. They are the same measurements, not independent replications.

publicationNotes.title: Formula flags re-measured
paragraphs: Four distinct formula rows are flagged: 10k parse-load p95, default-engine sorted text lookup, full-engine 1k parse-load and full-engine text lookup. Each was re-measured with the frozen harness's own workload factories, running every preceding workload in its original order, in 20 fresh processes per side: 10 interleaved ABBA blocks, 100 timed samples per row and side, on the full CPU mask.

Paired ratios, 0.6 / 0.5.4, with 99% block-bootstrap intervals: 10k parse-load median 0.987 [0.934, 1.041], p95 1.004 [0.940, 1.066]; full-engine 1k parse-load median 0.997 [0.927, 1.079], p95 1.039 [0.973, 1.118]; default-engine sorted text lookup median 1.044 [1.015, 1.077], p95 1.000 [0.883, 1.094]; full-engine text lookup median 1.128 [1.094, 1.170], p95 1.142 [1.086, 1.222].

The two parse-load flags did not reproduce. Text lookup is slower in 0.6: about 4% with the default engine and about 13% with the full engine. Both are within the 25% release budget, but they are real costs. Data: `bench/results/capture-attempts/formula-prefix-summary.json`, raw samples in `formula-prefix-10.json.gz`.
The separate paired formula gate passed all 52 rows at 8ac21089, using engine binaries that match ac4ab632 by SHA-256. Log: `bench/results/capture-attempts/formula-paired-gate.log`.

publicationNotes.title: Formula CPU affinity
paragraphs: Formula suites run on the full logical CPU mask on an otherwise quiet machine, as the 0.4.0 and 0.5.0 captures did. Earlier 0.6.0 attempts pinned the process to one CPU, then to two. Both starve JavaScriptCore's background WebAssembly compiler, which then competes with the timed work.

On one CPU, the 1k parse-load row split into fast and slow groups for both engines and failed the absolute gate twice. On two CPUs, XIRR after LINEST looked 44% slower; the same worker on the full mask measured 0.6 faster, with a paired ratio of 0.728 [0.651, 0.797]. These superseded captures and failed receipts remain under `bench/results/capture-attempts/` as diagnostics and are not mixed into these tables. No engine change, delay, JIT flag or relaxed budget was used.

These suites run in Bun, which uses JavaScriptCore. Most browsers running Sheetwrite use V8, whose WebAssembly compilation tiers differ, so cold-compilation effects measured here may not carry over to Chrome.

publicationNotes.title: Evidence handling
paragraphs: Capture receipts record command arguments without this machine's directories: a path inside the repository is repository-relative, and any other path keeps only its last segment under `<external>`. Four receipts captured before that rule had their arguments rewritten the same way; nothing else in them changed.

The 0.5.4 plain-formula baseline was captured a second time with a repository-relative output path, because the first capture wrote this machine's path into the result file. The replaced capture is kept as `capture-attempts/formula-before-portability-baseline.json.gz`, with machine directory prefixes replaced by placeholders.

The 0.6.0 captures ran on commit ac4ab632, which is not published because its tree holds receipts written before the argument rule above. Its packages are byte-identical to the 0.6.0 packages in this release; it differs only in benchmark tooling and results. The 0.5.4 baseline ran on dcfb2037, the 0.5.4 release branch before it was squash-merged; its packages are byte-identical to the published 0.5.4 release, 37fed9c7 on develop.

The 0.6.0 candidate is the release stack before its version bump, so raw package-version strings can still read 0.5.4; commits and loaded binary hashes identify the engines. Older committed 0.5.x results are history only, not comparison inputs.
